fills.researcher_notes: One question per company (gotcha 4), decided once for the whole Gulf South system and applied to every row in this brief that flags Operator (P5926, P5969): the current operator is Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC — a Boardwalk Pipeline Partners subsidiary, itself wholly owned by Loews Corporation since Boardwalk's 2018 take-private. Established from three independent origins: (1) Boardwalk's own current subsidiary page, 'Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC' (https://bwpipelines.com/subsidiaries/gulf-south-pipeline-company/home, verified); (2) Oil & Gas Journal, April 2026, 'FERC ... granted Gulf South Pipeline Co. LLC (Gulf South) authorization to build the $261 million Southeast Compression Utility and Reliability Expansion (SECURE) project' — trade press, independent of the applicant (verified, contains 'Gulf South Pipeline Co. LLC'); (3) a Federal Register notice naming 'Texas Gas Transmission, LLC; Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC' as the filing applicant on a 2025 docket (verified). Naming convention: I used 'Gulf South Pipeline Co LLC' (no comma, abbreviated 'Co') to match the exact string already on this system's operators/owners tab for P7784 in the same brief, rather than introducing a second spelling for one company — the sources above verify the full form 'Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC', which is the same entity. Note for the record: older SEC filings (2012 Form S-4) show the entity as 'Gulf South Pipeline Company, LP' — it converted from LP to LLC between 2013 and the 2019-2026 FERC filings I reviewed, which is presumably why the sheet's Operator cell was blank/stale. This is a company-identity fact, not a merger; no predecessor operator change applies here (Boardwalk itself was not acquired — it went private under its existing owner, Loews).
